name: mkdir
tldr: Creates a new directory (folder) in the current working location.

name: cd
tldr: Changes the current working directory to navigate between folders.

name: touch
tldr: Creates a new empty file in the current working directory.

name: ls
tldr: Lists all files and directories inside the current directory.

name: rm
tldr: Deletes specified files permanently from the file system.

name: clear
tldr: Clears all prior output and commands from the active terminal screen.

name: git init
tldr: Initializes a brand new Git repository and creates the hidden .git directory.

name: git status
tldr: Displays the state of the working directory and the staging area.

name: git add
tldr: Stages file modifications from the working directory for the next commit snapshot.
syntax:
git add <file_name>
git add .
git add -A

name: git commit
tldr: Takes a permanent snapshot of staged changes and records it to repository history.

name: git log
tldr: Displays chronological history of commits with their hashes, authors, and messages.
syntax:
git log
git log --oneline
git log -n <limit>

name: git branch
tldr: Lists, creates, or deletes branches to manage parallel development streams.
syntax:
git branch
git branch <branch_name>
git branch -d <branch_name>

name: git switch
tldr: Switches between branches to work on different features (modern alternative to git checkout).

name: git merge
tldr: Integrates changes from a target feature branch into your active branch.

name: git clone
tldr: Copies an existing remote repository onto your local machine with full commit history.

name: git remote
tldr: Manages tracked connections to remote repositories hosted on platforms like GitHub.
syntax:
git remote -v
git remote add <name> <url>
git remote remove <name>

name: git push
tldr: Uploads local committed snapshots to a remote repository branch.
syntax:
git push
git push -u <remote> <branch>
git push origin <branch>

name: git pull
tldr: Fetches updates from a remote repository and merges them directly into your current branch.

name: git fetch
tldr: Downloads commits and branches from the remote without merging them into your local work.

name: git restore
tldr: Restores working directory files from the last commit or unstages staged modifications.
